clue.text: Jasper spotted this green gem

parts.note: reads like a man named Jasper catching sight of a jewel, but jasper is a mineral, and the green variety flecked with red spots is the stone meant

explanation.surface: A man called Jasper notices a green jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jasper' looks like a person's name; it is the mineral, and 'spotted' describes the red flecks on it rather than seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: The gem is a dark green chalcedony or jasper marked with red spots that look like drops of blood.

clue.text: Association or Rugby game?

explanation.surface: A question about which football code is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: Association football and Rugby League are both codes of football; the word works as a union of clubs and as the thirteen-a-side rugby game.
explanation.definitionFit: An association of clubs or nations is a league, and one form of rugby is played under the name Rugby League.

clue.text: Do murals to order in Salisbury

indicators.note: made to order means rearranged as required, so these letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Commissioning wall paintings in an English cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to order' rearranges DO MURALS. OLD SARUM is the ancient hill-fort site of the original Salisbury, in Wiltshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical name of the first settlement at Salisbury, before the city moved down into the valley.

clue.text: Greeting from a sultan to one in distress

indicators.note: something in distress is in a bad way, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A ruler offers a welcome to a person in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' shuffles A SULTAN, TO and I (one) together.
explanation.definitionFit: A salutation is a formal word or gesture of welcome, a synonym for a hello.

clue.text: One of the problems with a large corporation

definitions.text: One of the problems with a large corporation

parts.words: One of the problems with a large corporation
parts.note: reads like a complaint about big business, but corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, so the trouble is bodily excess weight

explanation.surface: A management grumble about the difficulties of a huge company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is an old humorous British word for a large paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying a large belly is a sign of being very overweight, a medical condition.

clue.text: River bore on the move

indicators.note: letters on the move are shifting about, so this word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A tidal wave travels up a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the move' rearranges BORE. A bore is also a tidal wave in a river, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is a major river of northern Spain flowing into the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Rising man takes Indian tea — sounds diplomatic

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for man is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Sid is a man's name
the Cree are a Native American people
T sounds like tea, a standard crossword abbreviation

explanation.surface: A man on the up has a cup of Indian tea and speaks tactfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns SID into DIS, which then takes CREE (Indian) and T (tea). 'Indian' suggests India, but means a Native American. 'sounds' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tactful and careful not to give offence is what diplomacy requires.

clue.text: Bad article on German currency is irrelevant

parts.note: food that has gone bad is off
the definite article is the
the mark was the currency of Germany before the euro

explanation.surface: Complaining that a poorly written piece about the Deutschmark is beside the point.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark wide of the target is beside the point, not pertinent.

clue.text: Fail to justify fellow's confidence

parts.note: to belie something is to fail to fulfil or justify it
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: Someone lets down the trust another person placed in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confidence' here is trust or faith, not self-assurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith or trust in something is a firmly held conviction.

clue.text: The way the Spanish take part in auction for a little fish

indicators.note: the two pieces go to take their part inside the word for auction, so they are put within it

parts.note: a sale is an auction
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spaniards go to an auction to buy a small fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take part in' puts RD and EL inside SALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardelle is a small Mediterranean fish of the herring family, like a sardine or anchovy.

clue.text: Quicker way to produce a crop

explanation.surface: Advice on the fastest method of harvesting.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, a short cut is a brief haircut, which is what a crop is.
explanation.definitionFit: A quicker route saves time on a journey, and a cropped haircut is one kept close to the head.

clue.text: It's expensive to express sympathy with me

explanation.surface: Saying that something costly makes a person feel sorry for you.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the exclamation that, paired with 'me', makes a sympathetic 'Oh, ... me!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A costly item is high-priced, and the exclamation with 'me' is a stock phrase of pity or dismay.

clue.text: Stand down beside limo after crash

indicators.note: after a crash, the parts are scrambled, so these two words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A driver waits next to a wrecked limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after crash' rearranges BESIDE and LIMO together.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand troops down is to release them from military service at the end of a war.

clue.text: It helps to prevent hard water in the block!

definitions.text: It helps to prevent hard water in the block!

parts.words: It helps to prevent hard water in the block!
parts.note: reads like a water softener for an apartment block, but hard water is ice, and the block is a car engine block in winter

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a water softener in a block of flats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard water' suggests limescale; here it means water frozen solid, and 'block' is an engine block.
explanation.definitionFit: This additive lowers the freezing point of a car's coolant so it stays liquid in cold weather.

clue.text: Crammed naval hero into the hold

parts.note: something crammed is full
Horatio Nelson, victor at Trafalgar, is Britain's great naval hero

explanation.surface: A famous admiral is stuffed into a ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' looks like a ship's cargo space; it is a wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A full nelson is a wrestling grip with both arms under the opponent's armpits and hands clasped behind the neck.

clue.text: "And heard a on a dolphin's back" (M.N. Dream)

definitions.text: "And heard a on a dolphin's back" (M.N. Dream)

parts.words: "And heard a on a dolphin's back" (M.N. Dream)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Oberon's speech in A Midsummer Night's Dream, where a sea creature sings riding a dolphin

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints a dash after 'a' where the missing word goes; M.N. Dream is A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: In the play, Oberon recalls a half-woman, half-fish sea creature singing sweetly while seated on a dolphin.

clue.text: Cross supporter's abusive sound broadcast

indicators.note: the word for abusive is said aloud and heard as another word

parts.note: abusive language is rude
to beam a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: An angry fan's loud insults are carried on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' signals that RUDE (abusive) is heard as ROOD, an old word for the cross. 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: In a church, the rood beam is the timber across the chancel arch that carries the crucifix.

clue.text: Choose artist to appear in Greek tragedy

parts.note: to elect is to choose
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: Picking a painter for a part in an ancient Greek play.
explanation.definitionFit: Both Sophocles and Euripides wrote plays named after Agamemnon's daughter who avenges his murder.

clue.text: Beat music pounding out in the plant

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo or beat it

indicators.note: music pounded out is battered into a new shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Loud rhythmic music is played in a factory or works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat music' reads as one phrase; split it, CAP (beat) plus SICUM, the letters of MUSIC rearranged by 'pounding out'. 'plant' looks like a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: The pepper genus, including sweet and chilli peppers, is a flowering herb.

clue.text: Bound to run from a bumper

parts.note: to bound is to bounce
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Leaping away from a car's front fender.
explanation.walkthrough: A bumper in cricket is a short fast ball rising sharply at the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket uses both words for a short-pitched delivery that rears up toward the batter's head.

clue.text: Being mentally ill, subjected to analysis

explanation.surface: A patient is unwell and in therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is figures or a problem split into parts, not psychoanalysis.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has collapsed under strain is in a nervous collapse, and data divided into components has been analysed item by item.

clue.text: Mischievous child is hit with sticks

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster gets a caning.
explanation.walkthrough: The sticks are ice-hockey sticks striking the disc; the child is the sprite of A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The impish sprite in Shakespeare's play gives his name to any mischief-maker, and ice hockey is played with a rubber disc struck by sticks.

clue.text: Have a smoke in "Ring round the Moon'?

explanation.surface: Lighting up while watching a halo around the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A long straight-sided cigar is a type of smoke, and the halo of light seen around the moon is a luminous ring.

clue.text: Have no hesitation in stealing drink

indicators.note: to have no hesitation is to remove the word for it from the longer word

parts.note: liberating something is a jokey word for stealing it, so liberation is theft
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone helps themselves to a drink without a second thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have no' takes ER (hesitation) out of LIBERATION (stealing).
explanation.definitionFit: A libation is an offering of wine poured out, or jokingly any alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Day that is not ended.

indicators.note: with its ending cut off, the last letter of the phrase is lost

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A day that has no end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not ended' removes the last letter of ID EST. The Ides of March was the 15th, the day Caesar was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the Ides is the 15th of March, May, July and October and the 13th of other months.

clue.text: Realise stock — it is coming up for sale

definitions.text: it is coming up for sale

parts.note: to realise assets is to cash them in
crop and stock can both mean produce grown or held

explanation.surface: Selling off shares because they are on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' in the definition means growing out of the ground, not appearing at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers grow such produce to sell at market rather than to feed themselves.

clue.text: Meeting where the other side are invited to reply

definitions.text: Meeting where the other side are invited to reply

parts.words: Meeting where the other side are invited to reply
parts.note: sounds like a debate with an opposing party, but the other side is the spirit world, asked to answer by knocking

explanation.surface: A negotiation where the opposition is given a chance to answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other side' suggests opponents; it means the afterlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritualists hold such gatherings to contact the dead through a medium.

clue.text: Overripe pheasant, perhaps it's repulsive to most people

definitions.text: Overripe pheasant, perhaps it's repulsive to most people

parts.words: Overripe pheasant, perhaps it's repulsive to most people
parts.note: high game smells powerful, and the same phrase means anything too extreme or shocking for ordinary tastes

explanation.surface: Most diners cannot stomach well-hung game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Pheasant is hung until gamey; the phrase also comes from the Bible for teaching too hard for beginners.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-hung game is pungent food, and figuratively the phrase means material too harsh or radical for most audiences.
